discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall state)
subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological quantum materials
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator, classified by a Z2 invariant, and with Fu extended this to three-dimensional topological insulators. Molenkamp's group in 2007 observed quantized edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells, the first experimental realization of this new state of matter. The discovery introduced band topology as a universal organizing principle for ordinary crystalline solids, beyond the quantum Hall effect, and opened an entire field: three-dimensional topological insulators, the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulators, Weyl and Dirac semimetals, topological superconductors and axion electrodynamics. Its generality is shown by reproduction across many materials and laboratories worldwide. It also points to dissipationless edge transport and new spintronic functions for energy-efficient electronics. This is a landmark joining theory and materials experiment that has transformed condensed matter physics.
